vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a function clearStuckBalance_sender(uint256 amountPercentage) that allows authorized addresses (owner or authorized accounts) to withdraw a percentage of the contract's BNB balance directly to themselves. This is a classic owner privilege abuse vulnerability where privileged accounts can drain contract funds.
attack_strategy: Impersonate the owner (or an authorized address) and call clearStuckBalance_sender(100) to withdraw 100% of the contract's BNB balance to ourselves.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the contract owner. 2. Call clearStuckBalance_sender(100) on the target contract. 3. The contract will send its BNB balance to us (the attacker).

vulnerability_analysis: The contract allows the owner to transfer ownership to any address via transferOwnership(). Combined with clearStuckBalance_sender(), this allows privilege escalation and fund draining.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate current owner to transfer ownership to our test contract. 2. As the new owner, call clearStuckBalance_sender(100) to drain contract BNB to ourselves.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Get current owner address. 2. Impersonate current owner and call transferOwnership(address(this)). 3. As the new owner (our test contract), call clearStuckBalance_sender(100). 4. Verify our balance increased.
failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because when we impersonated the owner and called clearStuckBalance_sender(100), the BNB was sent to the owner's address (0xca07Df2Cbe0d98073e870b4325E969256924dd0f) instead of our test contract address. We need to first become the owner, then drain funds to ourselves.
